tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Open a project directory so later tools resolve project-relative paths against it. An explicit path overrides the client's `roots`, which override the server's working directory. This call validates the path and records it; it reads and writes nothing.

tools.name: diagnostics
tools.description: Compile TSX with the real front end and return the machine-readable diagnostics document of docs/specs/compiler-diagnostics-v1.md, byte-identical to `tessera_codegen --diagnostics-json` for the same input. With `source` it compiles that text in memory; without it, it compiles the whole open project folder.

source.description: The .tsx text to compile in memory. Omit it to compile the open project folder.

file.description: Project-relative name the diagnostics' spans are reported against, for example `ui/Counter.tsx`; defaults to `buffer.tsx`.

tools.name: get_ir
tools.description: Lower TSX and return its canonical IR JSON (docs/specs/ir-v1.md): the text of `source`, or the whole open project folder when `source` is omitted. Input that does not reach the IR returns the diagnostics document with `isError` instead of an empty module.

source.description: The .tsx text to lower. Omit it to lower the open project folder.

file.description: Project-relative name the diagnostics' spans are reported against, for example `ui/Counter.tsx`; defaults to `buffer.tsx`.

tools.name: generate
tools.description: Generate the C++ of the open project folder with the same driver as `tessera_codegen` (ADR-040). By default a dry run: it reports every generated file (size, SHA-256, `new`, `changed` or `unchanged`), the developer classes it would scaffold, and `exitCode` 1 when something differs, and writes nothing. With `write: true` it rewrites the generated bases inside the output directory (`codegen.outDir`, default `generated`) and scaffolds missing developer classes; it never modifies an existing developer file and never writes outside the project root. With `path` it returns that one generated file's text (always a dry run). A project with a blocking diagnostic returns the diagnostics document with `isError` and writes nothing.

write.description: Write the generated files. Omitted or false: dry run.

path.description: A generated file (`generated/App.g.hpp` or `App.g.hpp`): return its text instead of the summary.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List the files of the open project folder: project-relative path, kind (`source`, `style`, `config`, `theme`, `asset`, `other`), size, `readable` and a content digest. A file that is not accepted UI code, a `node_modules` or dot directory and a symbolic link are listed as `other` and never read. The folder is the opened project, else the client's first root, else the server's working directory; the result names `rootSource`.

tools.name: apply_edits
tools.description: Apply text edits to the open project in memory; `write: true` also writes them to the project directory. Never edits generated C++.

edits.description: Text edits to apply to the open project.

tools.name: set_viewport
tools.description: Set the preview viewport that later tools render at: `width`, `height`, `dpr` and the simulated foldable `foldPosture` (`flat`, `book`, `tabletop`). Omitted fields keep their value, as `viewport.set` does. The posture is data - no sensor, no clock - and reaches the same metrics and safe-area path the native app runs, so `snapshot` answers the document the studio previews for that posture.

width.description: Logical viewport width in pixels. Omitted: unchanged.

height.description: Logical viewport height in pixels. Omitted: unchanged.

foldPosture.description: Simulated foldable posture: `flat`, `book` (half-opened, vertical hinge) or `tabletop` (half-opened, horizontal hinge). Omitted: unchanged.

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: Return the harness UiSnapshot document (docs/specs/automation-ids-v1.md section 5.2) for the source, laid out at the viewport `set_viewport` last set. Byte-identical to the browser module's `tessera_scene_json_folded` for the same input.

source.description: The .tsx text to evaluate (in memory; no file is read).

file.description: Project-relative name the ids are hashed under; defaults to `ui/Preview.tsx`.

tools.name: query_style
tools.description: Return a node's computed style, matched rules (highest precedence first, with the cascade's own `overridden`) and layout box, as the studio's style inspector does. The source is laid out at the viewport `set_viewport` last set; a `uiId` no node carries answers `ok:false, reason:no_such_node`. A query: nothing is dispatched or changed.

source.description: The .tsx text to evaluate (in memory; no file is read).

file.description: Project-relative name the ids are hashed under; defaults to `ui/Preview.tsx`.

uiId.description: The decimal UiId of the node to inspect, as `snapshot` lists it.

tools.name: pick
tools.description: Return the node at a point in the preview: its automation id, element kind and box, found with the input router's own hit test, so it is the node a press there would reach. `x` and `y` are logical viewport pixels, the space `snapshot`'s bounds are in. A point over no node answers `found:false`. A query: nothing is dispatched or changed.

source.description: The .tsx text to evaluate (in memory; no file is read).

file.description: Project-relative name the ids are hashed under; defaults to `ui/Preview.tsx`.

x.description: Point x in logical viewport pixels.

y.description: Point y in logical viewport pixels.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Render the scene and return a PNG. Best-effort visual evidence, never a golden.

tools.name: run_script
tools.description: Run a harness script (launch/click/assert/...) and return its report document.

script.description: The harness script document to run.
